steps.text: The step grid is sixteen sixteenth-notes — one bar of 4/4. A lit step sounds when the playhead reaches it. Everything loops, so a tiny idea becomes a groove.
steps.title: STEPS

steps.text: Watch — I'll put a kick drum note (C2) on step 1. Low notes are felt more than heard; that's the kick's whole job.
steps.title: KICK

steps.text: Your turn: light up steps 5, 9 and 13 with the same low note. Click a step, or press Ctrl+1..0 after picking the octave. Four kicks, evenly spaced — that's house music's heartbeat.
steps.title: FOUR ON THE FLOOR

steps.text: Now some hats on the offbeats — steps 3, 7, 11, 15. Pick a high note (try F#5, key 78). Offbeats push the groove forward; that's syncopation, and it's the whole trick.
steps.title: HATS

steps.text: Press play. You just programmed a beat — kick on the quarters, hats on the offbeats. Mute a step and feel the groove sag; that's how much the little notes matter.
steps.title: PLAY

steps.text: That's lesson one: a loop, a low anchor, offbeat energy. Every beat you'll ever make is this idea with better sounds and braver choices.
steps.title: DONE
